Street guides / 04

What kind of food does the sign suggest?

You can guess a restaurant's focus without reading every line of its menu.

Updated 2 October 2026

식당

Understand the place

식당 is a general word for a restaurant. Other signs name food or a style of eating: 김밥 is seaweed rice rolls, 국수 is noodles, and 분식 commonly points to casual Korean snacks and simple meals. 치킨 often signals a fried-chicken shop in a restaurant setting.

Easy to mix up

김밥 on a sign does not mean the shop sells only gimbap. 분식 is a category, not one dish. A sign can suggest a specialty, but it cannot tell you every ingredient or whether an item suits your dietary needs. Check the menu or ask the staff for those details.

A sign you might see

김밥 · 분식

A storefront reads 김밥 · 분식. Expect a casual food place and start looking for the menu, rather than treating the two words as the name of a single meal. If you see 국수 nearby, you have spotted another food clue: noodles.

Try it on your next walk

Imagine you want noodles. Find 국수 among the signs, listen to it, and then try the food round. For a second challenge, explain the difference between 식당 and 김밥 in your own words.
